dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: Thanks for filling it out. We give this form to everyone once a year regardless of why they come in. It helps us provide better care. Is it okay if I take a look at what you put down?

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Sure.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: So, let's see. It looks that you put-- You drink alcohol at least four times a week on average-

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Mm-hmm.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: -and you usually have three to four drinks when you do drink.

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Usually three drinks and glasses of wine.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: Okay. That's at least 12 drinks a week.

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Something like that.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: Okay. Just so you know, my role, um, when we talk about alcohol use, is just to share information about risk and to help patients who want help. This is different than telling them what I think they should do. I don't do that.

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Okay.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: Uh, what else can you tell me about your drinking.

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Well, I usually drink when I'm at home trying to unwind and I drink while I'm watching a movie. And sometimes, um, I take a bath but I also drink when I take a bath sometimes.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: Okay. So, can I share with you some information on alcohol use?

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Okay.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: Okay. So, there has been a lot of research on alcohol use and the guidelines we use in this country says that having seven or more drinks per week can raise the risk of health problems for women.

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Hmm. Seven?

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: Seven.

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Wow. I knew my doctor didn't like me drinking the amount that I did but I didn't know that seven was the limit.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: Yeah, you're surprised to hear that?

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Yes. What-what kind of health problems?

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: Well things like heart disease, cancer, liver problems, uh, stomach pains, insomnia. Unfortunately, uh, people who drink at a risky level are more likely to be diagnosed with depression and alcohol can make depression worse or harder to treat.

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Hmm. Well, that's not good news.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: Well, how do you think your drinking relates to the depression you've experienced?

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Well, to be honest, I drink sometimes when I'm feeling down and I find it more interesting and not so blur.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: Okay. And how do you feel after you drink?

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Well, then I feel blur again.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: So, there are some answers on this form here. Uh, less than monthly you drank more than you intended to.

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Yes on occasion.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: And sometimes you feel guilty after you drink.

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Sometimes I just don't like how much I drink. I sometimes finish a bottle in one night.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: So you're not proud of finishing a bottle?

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: No, it's not like I get crazy or anything but I just don't like the amount that I'm drinking.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: Right. By the way, binge drinking is defined for women as having more than, uh, three drinks and there are about five drinks in a bottle. So, you enjoy drinking wine because it helps make things, uh, a little bit more interesting when you're feeling down but at the same time you don't like drinking when you have more than you want it to and then the depression returns after you drink.

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Mm-hmm. Yes, sometimes I feel worse after drinking.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: Where do you wanna go from here? What do you wanna change about your drinking habits?

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Well, I don't think that I'm ready to cut down to seven drinks a week. That seems like a lot but I would consider cutting back to two drinks a night. I think that would be my goal.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: If I gave you a scale from 0 to 10, 0 being not ready at all to cut back on drinking and 10 being very ready, what number would you be at?

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: I'd say an eight.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: Okay. Why do you think it's not something less like a six?

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Well, I'm more ready than a six because I'm ready to cut back on my drinking and I don't wanna make my depression any worse.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: What would help you cut back to two drinks?

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Maybe having less wine in the house.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: Having less wine in the house will help?

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Yes.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: What else besides drinking helps you relax and unwind in the evenings?

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Well, I like to watch movies, read a book, and take a bath but sometimes I drink when I take a bath.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: So, it's not just wine that helps you relax. Um, there's reading a book, watching a movie, and taking a hot bath too.

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Mm-hmm. Yes.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: Okay. So, it sounds like you have some reasons to cut back on drinking and you have ways to relax besides drinking and it sounds like you're pretty ready to cut back.

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Yes.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: Great. I'd be interested to see how well you do on your goal in the next few weeks. Would you be willing to come back and talk to me about it?

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Sure.

dialog.speaker: therapist
dialog.text: Great. So, let's see how well you're doing with these new meds.

dialog.speaker: patient
dialog.text: Okay.
